comparator.name: Zorg, Gezondheid & Samenleving
comparator.academicYear: Current Utrecht University 2026–2027 curriculum and OER, checked 2026-09-28
comparator.sourceNotes: The official programme and student curriculum pages describe a three-year, 180-EC full-time bachelor. The current student page specifies 150 EC of regular education and 30 EC of profiling space; years 1 and 2 are compulsory, year 3 begins with four compulsory courses and ends with profiling space plus the Societal Challenge final project. Because the public pages name courses and programme-level credit totals without assigning a visible EC value to every individual course, this reconstruction preserves the authoritative 60-EC first year, 60-EC second year, 30-EC compulsory first half of year 3 and 30-EC combined profiling/final-project segment instead of inventing per-course credits.

components.name: Year 1 compulsory interdisciplinary health curriculum
components.note: Vroege ontwikkeling; Zorgsystemen in een veranderende samenleving; Systemen op moleculair niveau; Vergelijkende bouw en functie; Denken en denkers; Mechanismen van ziek en gezond 1; and Verkenning samenleving.

components.name: Year 2 compulsory interdisciplinary health curriculum
components.note: Wetenschap voor academische professionals; Microben en infecties; Mechanismen van ziek en gezond 2; Kwantitatief denken voor zorgprofessionals; Gezondheidszorg en samenleving; Principes van interventie en therapie; Mentale gezondheid en gedrag; and Technologie en innovatie in de gezondheidszorg.

components.name: Year 3 compulsory first-half curriculum
components.note: Dilemmas in de praktijk; Biotechnologie; Gezonde omgeving; and Ontsporing en veroudering.

components.name: Year 3 profiling space and Societal Challenge
components.note: The programme-level 30-EC profiling space is combined here with the Societal Challenge final-project requirement because the current public curriculum page does not expose a separate per-component EC split.

questionsApplications.label: How do biological, behavioural and social systems interact in health and disease?
How should technology and intervention be evaluated and used responsibly in future healthcare?
How can prevention, policy and environmental change improve human, animal and population health?

alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines biomedical and behavioural foundations with anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, cell biology, pathology, immunology, pharmacology, neuroscience, health psychology, epidemiology, sociology and research methods. It connects health and disease mechanisms to behaviour and society, while remaining an academic liberal-arts-and-sciences curriculum rather than a clinical or professionally qualifying healthcare programme.

alternatives.labelRationale: The route retains a substantial biomedical and behavioural core while adding programming, data science, machine learning, medical imaging, robotics and AI ethics. The label states this interdisciplinary direction without claiming a dedicated clinical-technology qualification.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route removes dedicated epidemiology, anatomy, molecular cell biology, biochemistry, infection and immunity, neurobiology, abnormal psychology, medical and health psychology, sociology, psychodiagnostics and lifespan psychology. It adds programming, mathematical methods, introductory and advanced data science, machine learning, computer vision, databases, algorithms, linear algebra, robotics and AI ethics. Thirteen courses are shared and eleven differ, shifting the organising logic from broad biomedical and behavioural study to computation and emerging healthcare technology.

alternatives.concept: A population-health route connecting epidemiology, prevention and biopsychosocial health with quantitative and qualitative research, ethics, public economics, behavioural policy, organisational leadership, sociology, sustainability governance and public communication.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route removes the anatomy, cell biology, physiology, biochemistry, laboratory, pathology, immunology, mechanisms-of-disease, pharmacology, neurobiology, cognitive-neuroscience and psychodiagnostics sequence. It adds ethics, qualitative research, public and behavioural economics, organisational and diversity leadership, modern and contemporary sociology, sustainability governance, international-relations theory and persuasive communication. Eleven courses are shared with the closest match and six with the technology route. Its organising logic is prevention, populations, institutions and policy rather than biomedical mechanisms or technology development.

progressionAssessment.rationale: The first semester establishes biomedical, behavioural, epidemiological and professional foundations. Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine precedes every selected life-science and biomedical course that formally requires it; Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes all selected advanced cognition and psychology courses that require it. Research Methods & Statistics and the laboratory course precede the advanced statistical and evidence-synthesis work conceptually. The final four semesters progress through normal structure and function into pathology, immunity, treatment, higher cognition, health psychology, psychodiagnostics and advanced research. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme’s integrated health-and-disease, cross-disciplinary and care-and-society interests. Two further coherent directions remain. Explicit interests in technology, future healthcare and ethical challenges support a health-technology, data and AI route; explicit interests in prevention, epidemics, greener healthcare, living environments and population health support a public-health, policy and society route. All three schedules are feasible and substantively distinct: the closest and technology routes share 13 courses, the closest and public-health routes share 11, and the technology and public-health routes share 6. The maximum of three alternatives is therefore reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both provide broad foundations in normal biological systems, health and disease; the comparator integrates these with pharmaceutical, veterinary and societal perspectives.

Both address ethical and professional reasoning; the comparator’s third-year core includes practice dilemmas and cross-disciplinary professional contexts.

notes.text: The Utrecht programme is a deliberately integrated, small-scale curriculum spanning human and animal health, pharmacy, healthcare practice, professional development and a Societal Challenge final project. UCR can assemble strong biomedical, behavioural, population-health, policy and technology pathways, but it does not reproduce that fixed professional context, its medical-pharmaceutical-veterinary integration, practice placements or programme-wide assessment model. These are academically related alternatives, not substitutes for the named degree.
